resources.string:
Free and open source voices are built by the free software community and distributed separately.

CuevaReader is also built only with free and open source software. We believe in the benefits of software freedom: you can use, study, share and improve every part of it, and nobody pays royalties or license fees to anyone.

Many apps could be built this way with little effort, but most are not. We hope this encourages you to create and prefer using open source alternatives.
CuevaReader reads books aloud using a free, open source text-to-speech engine. It is not bundled with the app, so please install one of these first:

1. Tap "Download" next to an engine. Its F-Droid page opens in your browser.
2. Scroll down and tap "Download APK" on the latest version (or install it through the F-Droid app if you have it).
3. Open the downloaded file from the notification or your Downloads folder.
4. If Android asks, allow your browser to "Install unknown apps", then go back and tap Install.
5. Open the engine app once and download a voice for your language (SherpaTTS and RHVoice need this).
6. Come back to CuevaReader and tap the button below.

Supported limits are files up to 100 MB, PDFs up to 500 pages, and DOCX text up to 20 MB.

You can find free books in the public domain. CuevaReader lets you read and listen to EPUB, PDF and DOCX book files with extractable text.

To add a book:
1. Download it as an EPUB, PDF or DOCX. You will usually find it in Downloads.
2. Open the file and choose CuevaReader. You can also select it using Open book inside the app.
3. If you open it from another app and have a writable library folder configured, CuevaReader will offer to move it there. If Android does not allow deleting the original, it will save a copy. You can then find it in Library.

PDF and DOCX files are read directly by extracting their text, without converting them to EPUB or saving an EPUB. Images and optical character recognition (OCR) for scanned pages are not included.

MOBI and AZW files are not supported. You can convert DRM-free files to EPUB using Calibre on a computer. Download Calibre: https://calibre-ebook.com/download

Create or select your library folder

CuevaReader lists the EPUB books stored in a folder of your choice. We suggest a folder called "Reader" in your internal storage.

In the next screen:
1. If you are not in the internal storage root, open the menu (☰) and pick your phone's storage.
2. Tap ⋮ and choose "New folder", name it Reader (skip this if it already exists).
3. Open the Reader folder and tap "Use this folder", then "Allow".

You can change the folder later from the Library panel.
